conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and close to net zero. Counterparties that reported after GPC's July 21 call show industrial demand speeding up (Fastenal Q3 +15.5% daily sales, heavy manufacturing about +20%, ISM 54.5) against a Motion consensus of only +4.9%, and auto commercial demand is firm (AutoZone domestic commercial +8.6%). Against that, diesel set a record $6.29 in September, 27% above July, after GPC had guided only $20-30M of Iran/fuel cost for the rest of the year, and European aftermarket peer LKQ cut its guide after GPC raised its International outlook. The findings sum to +0.10. p_up is 51 on abs 5.5, giving +0.11. The two measurements agree that there is no edge here. This name sells beats when the auto guide wobbles (July -2.7% on the baseline basis and about -7% in the wire; February -14.6%), which keeps p_up near 50.

findings.finding: Industrial distributors that reported after GPC's July 21 call show MRO demand speeding up through Q3. Fastenal Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-14): daily sales +15.5% y/y, heavy manufacturing about +20%, other manufacturing about +13%, pricing only about 240bp, and management said industrial conditions 'continued to improve in Q3'. ISM manufacturing was 54.5 in September (new orders 55.3, backlog 56.4, prices 77.9), the ninth straight month of expansion. Against this, consensus has Motion/Industrial at $2.38B, +4.9% y/y, which is a slowdown from Q2's +7.1% (comps +6.1%). The Industrial FY guide of +3-6% has not moved. Motion is about 37% of sales and about 47% of segment EBITDA, and Industrial EBITDA consensus is already $314M (+10.2%). So a sales beat of 2-3 points, roughly $50-70M, adds perhaps $10-15M of EBITDA, or $0.05-0.08 of EPS, plus a case for raising the Industrial guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 Industrial grew +7.1% (comps +6.1%, EBITDA +9.8%), beating, yet the stock fell on the auto guide trim (-2.68% on the baseline basis, about -7% in the wire). Industrial strength has not offset auto weakness in the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side Industrial sales estimates still imply a slowdown to +4.9%, below Q2's run-rate, three months after Q2 and with ISM still rising. If the market had priced the peer acceleration, the Industrial bar would sit at or above +7%. The stock has risen only 4.4% in 20 days.

findings.finding: Fuel costs rose well past the level GPC guided around. BTS: September 2026 diesel averaged a record $6.29/gal, up 15.2% m/m, 67.8% y/y and 27% above July's $4.96. Regular gasoline averaged $4.36, up 7.3% m/m and 37.6% y/y, against $3.93 in July. On July 21 GPC said the Iran conflict cost about $16M of EBITDA in Q2, almost all in Automotive. It guided only $20-30M of incremental cost for the whole rest of 2026, which is below the Q2 run-rate, so it assumed easing. GPC also said June NAPA sales were roughly flat because of higher fuel prices, and it cut the Automotive outlook on consumer sentiment. The guidance risk from fuel continuing to rise is Automotive freight and delivery cost plus DIY softness. A $10-20M overrun is $0.05-0.10 of EPS and pressures the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: an EPS beat, but the Automotive outlook was trimmed on fuel and consumer sentiment and the GAAP guide was cut; the stock fell (-2.68% on the baseline basis, about -7% in the wire, https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/07/60584481). February 2026: -14.56% on the initial FY guide. This name trades on the auto guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has been unchanged for 30 days (AlphaStreet), the FY street number of $7.73 sits at the guide midpoint, and the stock rose 4.4% into the print. None of this reflects a cost assumption overtaken by a record diesel spike. If it were priced, estimates would have drifted down or the put skew would be bid; skew is +0.97, close to flat.
findings.independence: GPC's sensitivity and assumption come from the Q2 call transcript, a different document: https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176 (2026-07-21). findings.finding: Auto aftermarket peers that reported after GPC show commercial (DIFM) demand firm and improving through the summer. AutoZone FQ4 (16 weeks to 2026-08-29): domestic commercial sales +8.6%, total domestic comps +1.6%, DIY -0.6%, and management said sales bottomed in June and improved as the quarter went on. O'Reilly Q2 (reported 2026-07-29): professional comps about +10%, DIY hot-weather categories 'reversed strongly' in July, FY comp guide raised to 4-6%. NAPA is about 80% commercial, and consensus has North America Automotive at only +2.9% ($2.56B), against Q2's +3.8% (comps +2.6%) and a 2.5-4.5% FY guide. So the NA auto line looks achievable to slightly beatable. NAPA has lagged peers (Q2 commercial comps about +4%), so the read-through is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA Auto is the line the stock traded on in July 2026 (trimmed growth guide, stock down) and February 2026 (-14.56%). An in-line NA auto quarter with a held guide in October 2025 gave +2.05%.
findings.why_not_priced: The NA Auto bar of +2.9% sits near the low end of GPC's own 2.5-4.5% guide, so the street has not moved toward the peers' strength. AutoZone's commercial acceleration post-dates GPC's last call. If the market had priced it, NA Auto estimates would sit nearer 3.5-4%.

findings.finding: International Automotive has been raised into a weakening European backdrop. On July 21 GPC raised its International Auto sales guide from +3-6% to +5-8% (Q2: +8.2%, of which comps +0.6% and FX +4.9%). Nine days later, on 2026-07-30, LKQ cut its FY adjusted EPS guide from $2.90-3.20 to $2.60-2.90 and its parts organic revenue guide to -1% to -3%, citing weaker European demand (UK, Benelux) plus its own German ERP problems; its stock fell about 16% premarket. EUR/USD also slipped from about 1.16 in early September to about 1.147-1.15 mid-September, against roughly 1.17 a year earlier, which erodes the FX tailwind that carried most of the raise. GPC itself said Europe was 'choppy but sequentially improving' and pointed to the UK and Germany. LKQ's German problems may hand share to GPC's European business, so the net risk is modest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International Auto has not been the line GPC traded on in the baseline prints; NA auto and the EPS guide dominated.
findings.why_not_priced: LKQ's cut came after GPC's call, and the International bar implied by Zacks segment estimates (about $1.57B) still assumes growth near the raised guide. If the market had priced it, the International estimate would have been trimmed.
findings.independence: FX from a different source: https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/USD-EUR-2026. GPC's own July comments cut against this: https://www.webull.com/news/15265626932274176.

findings.finding: GPC's own July guidance points to H2 support. It expected 'another very solid Q3' and accelerating gross margin expansion in H2 from sourcing, pricing and easier acquisition comparisons. Cost savings were $55M year to date ($30M in Q2, about $0.16/share), against a 2026 target of $100-125M, which implies $45-70M in H2. Management said the year would otherwise be tracking toward the high end of the $7.50-8.00 range. All of this sits inside the guide the market was told to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat on adjusted EPS ($2.15 vs $2.08) partly on savings, and the stock was sold anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it is the company's own public guidance, and the street FY number of $7.73 sits at the midpoint.
findings.independence: Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40987/000004098726000031/gpc-earnq22026.htm (the same event, a different document).

findings.finding: The separation is going ahead and a NAPA sale looks off. The 8-K of 2026-09-09 named Court Carruthers CEO-elect of GPC (the auto business), with Will Stengel to lead Motion. Bert Nappier added COO to his CFO role. Separate Investor Days are set for 2026-12-08 (GPC) and 2026-12-09 (Motion), and closing is targeted for Q1 2027. This effectively answers the July reports of a roughly $10B O'Reilly bid for NAPA in favour of the spin. The Q3 call is therefore unlikely to carry standalone 2027 targets, which are deferred to December. That lowers the odds of a large guidance shock on this print rather than giving it a direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: February 2026, the split announcement plus the FY guide: -14.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was public on September 9 and is priced. It is filed as context for the size of the move.

findings.finding: GPC filed an S-3ASR automatic shelf on 2026-10-16. This is the routine three-year renewal of its WKSI shelf: earlier ones were filed in October 2020 and on 2023-10-20, and the 2023 shelf expires about now. Asking what the money buys: nothing specific is disclosed. Debt allocation for the Motion spin (Term Loan A, an undrawn $500M delayed-draw loan, $683M of commercial paper at June 30) is the plausible use. It is not a distress signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior renewals (October 2020, October 2023) did not move the stock on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and routine; the zero size says it is not a finding of mispricing.

baseline_tension: The findings net to roughly zero, which matches a flat skew (+0.97) and a modest +4.4% run-up. The industrial positive and the fuel-cost negative cut in opposite directions, and nothing contradicts the 'balanced' lean.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its Q2 beat on the auto guide): the industrial finding goes from +1.2 to +1.0 and p_up from 52 to 51.

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a small finding): the fuel/diesel finding goes from -1.0 to -0.9. It was kept because GPC itself quantified its sensitivity ($16M in Q2) and an assumption below the run-rate.
Rules 5/9 (peer proxy; NAPA's lag behind peers): the auto commercial read-through goes from +0.6 to +0.5, and AAP DIY from -0.3 to -0.2, net of retail being about 20% of NAPA.

Rule 3 (own caveat must reach the number): International Auto goes from -0.6 to -0.4, because GPC's own 'sequentially improving' Europe comment and LKQ's self-inflicted German ERP problems argue against it.
Rule 6 (inside the company's guide): the cost-savings/H2 margin finding goes from +0.3 to +0.1. The EPS bar is disputed ($2.04-2.10), which keeps every EPS-dependent size small.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the S-3ASR was checked as a routine three-year WKSI renewal and stays at 0.
Rule 7: short interest was checked (4.8% of float, 6.9 DTC, falling) before the negatives; it is not crowded, so they were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
Rule 2: the tariff-refund one-off was already rejected by document before the lessons were read; nothing changed there.
